To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the brain may have evolved to efficiently learn to predict the future from past sensory input and that this process may be the basis for the hierarchy of neuronal tuning properties along the visual pathway.

(1) a single normative model can account for the hierarchy from retina to MT of tuning to dynamic visual inputs and (2) that the model learns to represent features that are predictive of future sensory input.
hierarchical temporal prediction captures the hierarchical tuning to dynamic inputs from retina to cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the brain represents the visual environment.
understanding the nature of visual representations in the brain and how these change along the visual processing pathway.
the question of how neurons in the brain encode information about visual stimuli, and more specifically, how the brain represents the motion of objects in our visual field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain is not a general coding principle, but it is not a general code.
the brain has evolved to represent the features that best predict the future.
the brain may be a general purpose learning machine that learns to predict the future based on the past.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain may have evolved to represent features that efficiently predict the future, and that the hierarchy of tuning properties in the visual cortex may reflect this.

hierarchical temporal prediction is an effective framework to explain the hierarchy of tuning from retina to MT cortex, and it can account for the diversity of neuronal response properties along the visual pathway.
the brain is not designed to represent the world, but rather, the world as it changes over time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain may use hierarchical temporal prediction as a general principle for representing features that are useful for predicting the future from the past.
the visual system is organized to predict the future.
a simple normative model can explain a wide variety of neuronal responses in visual cortex, and in particular the hierarchy of tuning properties along the pathway.
